param: standard background step on the judgment surface (one knob: none vs siril subsky 1, the registry's MW-safe first-degree plane)
hypothesis: the industry-standard background-extraction stage removes the corner chroma the user flagged (pre-BGE state)
verdict: PARTIAL/needs-eyes - the degree-1 plane removed the ONE-SIDED term (TR 1.070->1.057; corners now uniform ~5.5%) at zero structure cost (NAN contrast identical - dust-safe NULL), but CANNOT remove the remaining RADIAL ~5% R/G term: a plane has no radial component. The radial residue is the per-channel calibration class (flat error x ~5x corner amplification at 2.4 EV falloff), whose dust-safe fix is upstream (real per-channel flats), not any background model this MW-filling class tolerates (registry: degree>=2 and full BGE eat the MW).

verdict: WIN - corners collapse to july14-class neutral (1.008-1.018) on every product; K scatter collapses 5x; the user-flagged 'fake red' was the chain's ICC toe injection, level-gated to the 3s class. Surfaces awaiting the user's eyes.

param: one knob: Siril `seqsubsky 1` on the dark-subtracted source frames before they are stacked into the sky flat (build_sky_flat --desky). Everything else identical: same 401 frames, same master dark, same rej=wins, same -norm=mul.
hypothesis: the sky flat bakes in sky-brightness structure fixed in the ALT-AZ frame (moonlight, airmass) because on a FIXED mount the camera is horizon-fixed too, so that gradient does not drift across the sensor and does not reject out. Since it enters ADDITIVELY through the frames, removing it additively PER FRAME is the matching domain — and it must not touch vignetting, PRNU or dust.

single_frame_probe.note: Siril logs 'computed for CFA image' — mosaic-aware

verdict: WIN on the target term, with a stated ceiling. The sky/odd plane drops 4.84% -> 1.98% (-59%) while everything the flat exists to carry is preserved: radial vignetting to <=0.11% (measured within ONE Bayer phase — the mixed-phase measure reads +0.95% and is CONFOUNDED by the 59.9% inter-phase spread), PRNU correlation 0.999951, dust-class mote depth -3.4% at correlation 0.9868, specks 0. The residual ~2% is NOT reachable by this method: a sky gradient across a 28.6 deg field has CURVATURE, and degree 1 removes only the linear part while degree >=2 is a measured dead end (erases the MW at this focal length). So ~59% is near the MW-safe ceiling. The -3.4%/0.1% shifts are level-normalisation side effects, not structure loss (correlations rule that out). CAVEAT: n=1 set; confirm on a second set before making --desky the default, and note that adopting it does NOT retroactively clean existing products — realising the benefit needs the affected sets rebuilt.

param: OBSERVATION, not a new arm: the SPCC K delta produced by inserting the background step (per-frame subsky 1 + de-skied flat) ahead of SPCC. README's reference-standard table names this delta as THE check on the repo's claim that per-star local-annulus photometry cancels a smooth background, so the K fit is order-robust. The data existed in the branch's own records and was never compared.
control: the pre-desky SPCC records on the same fields
hypothesis: if the K fit is order-robust, inserting a background step upstream leaves K within the chain's own K scatter
verdict: NEEDS-EYES / NOT CONFIRMED. K_G moves -1.20% (set-01) and -1.48% (combine), K_B -0.47% and -0.80%, on essentially unchanged star counts (5109->5110, 5286->5286). That is LARGER than the chain's own recorded K_G scatter of 0.006 (0.9%, the icc_leg_fix_rebuild post-family), so the order-robustness claim is NOT confirmed by this data. CONFOUNDED and that is the honest reading: the de-skied arm also removes a real ~3% multiplicative object tilt, which legitimately changes measured star colours, so this cannot separate 'SPCC is order-sensitive' from 'the calibration genuinely changed'. Separating them needs SPCC run on the SAME stack with and without an on-stack background step only - one knob, no calibration change. Until then, treat order-robustness as UNTESTED rather than verified.

seqsubsky_dither.note: seqsubsky DITHERS BY DEFAULT (opposite of subsky) and the dither is UNSEEDED — two runs of the identical command differ by sigma 0.4 ADU (+-1.0) while -nodither runs are bit-identical (Siril isub all-nil). Both --desky call sites now pin -nodither. The flats built before the pin differ by 0.4/sqrt(401) = 0.02 ADU = 0.047% of sky, BELOW the chain's 0.073% flat-sky run-to-run floor, so they need no rebuild.

verdict: CONFIRMED on n=2 — the caveat is closed. Odd plane falls 59% (set-01) and 69% (set-02); specks 1 vs 1 on both, a clean NULL. Two evidence defects found and corrected in the process (the speck gate could not fail; the background step was unseeded), neither of which changes the direction of the result. WHICH ARM IS CORRECT is still not settled by this — see BACKLOG item 20 for the cross-position star-flux test.

starnet2_via_siril.cli_pinning_available: none — I/O, weights, stride, upsample only

full_chain_repeat.note: a full re-render reproduced both ratios exactly

verdict: HYPOTHESIS REFUTED — the render tier is BIT-REPRODUCIBLE end to end on this rig, so byte-identity is the available bar and nothing needed pinning. CONSEQUENCE: the 1.34% 'run-to-run floor' previously hardcoded into the render colour verdict was a MISATTRIBUTION — it came from two render records read as a same-arm repeat, where the earlier record logged neither its linear source nor its knob provenance. Removed; the colour check now reports an EXACT shift with no NULL-below-floor verdict, because with a deterministic chain there is no floor to hide an effect under and any difference between two ladder arms off one stack is the knob. Lesson recorded: a floor is a MEASUREMENT, not a subtraction of two numbers you happen to have.

param: WHAT the frame-filling faint structure in july23 set-01+02 actually is — the term 'cosmic dust / MW / IFN' the repo protects under 'dust-safe' doctrine is never defined and was never independently identified. External predictor: Gaia DR3 integrated flux per cell (ESA TAP, 2,985,425 sources G<17 over the footprint). Pixel measure: Siril stat on a uniform 14x10 lattice of 300 px cells, on three surfaces of the approved render (linear SPCC stack / StarNet2 star layer / StarNet2 starless layer).
control: pre-desky stack (stack_set-01+02_min_spcc.fit — same frames, no per-frame seqsubsky 1, non-de-skied flat) as the background-step control; NGC 7000 and IC 1318 as pre-registered positive controls; Gaia source COUNT as the competing predictor against Gaia FLUX
hypothesis: the diffuse field at 17"/px in the galactic plane is UNRESOLVED STARLIGHT, not diffuse nebulosity; real dust reads as silhouette. Pre-registered in sessions/july23/work/dustprobe/HYPOTHESIS.txt with the falsifying numbers stated before the run.

metrics.detection_limit_method: one-to-one mutual-nearest Gaia match + 90in isolation cut; the naive many-to-one first pass fitted slope 0.39 where physics demands 1.0, clean matching restored 0.96-0.97

verdict: HYPOTHESIS SUPPORTED, with a correction neither position anticipated. (1) The frame-filling faint structure IS unresolved starlight: the StarNet2 star layer's per-cell MEDIAN — its diffuse floor — tracks Gaia's unresolved-starlight prediction at R2 0.9631, and UNRESOLVED flux (R2 0.963) beats TOTAL flux (R2 0.503), so it is the unresolved population specifically, not brightness or crowding generally. This data resolves only to G~11.0 and the field carries ~0.2 catalogued sources per PIXEL brighter than G=17 — it is confusion-limited, so most Milky Way starlight here structurally cannot appear as stars. (2) The correction: the render chain ALREADY removes that starlight, at the SEPARATION stage. The star layer carries 0.916x the total catalogued starlight and 1.91x the resolved-only prediction. What remains — the 'starless' layer the dust-safe doctrine protects — ANTI-correlates with starlight (slope -0.319, R2 0.567) and is colour-neutral to R/G 1.0022 +- 0.0048 across the whole frame. It is the residual left after the Milky Way was taken out, not the Milky Way. (3) Real diffuse emission IS present and measurable, but localized: NGC 7000 sits +2.5 sd above the starlight relation and reads R/G 1.1918 in the STAR layer against a 0.9303 field — so its Ha lands in the star layer too. (4) NOT a background-step artifact: the two stack arms agree (slope 0.301 desky vs 0.287 pre-desky). NOT settled here: whether the haze should be removed (aesthetic, the user's eyes on PNG16 finals), and the absolute ADU scale, which carries a 20-30% systematic from Gaussian-fit photometry on trailed stars — every correlation above is scale-free and unaffected.

new_entries: terminology entry defining the four senses with their measurements
star_asinh dead end with the 44x dynamic-range compression number

verdict: DOCTRINE CORRECTED. The diffuse field at 17"/px is UNRESOLVED STARLIGHT (R2 0.9631 vs Gaia, detection limit G~11.0, ~0.2 catalogued sources/px to G=17), not a dust complex. HII regions (NGC 7000, IC 1318) are emission and were being lumped in with it. Real dust appears as SILHOUETTE (the Cygnus Rift, visible in Gaia's own flux deficit on the plane). Optical dust motes are a flat-field feature and the only correct prior use of the word. Every mechanism MEASUREMENT in the registry stands unchanged — only the attribution was wrong, and the corrections say so explicitly rather than rewriting history. Rendering rule established: unresolved starlight is rendered AS STARS with its brightness hierarchy intact, never amplified as a diffuse glow; raising star_asinh to do so is now a dead end with its numbers.
